UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile for individuals (couples) interacting with the marketplace, primarily for sending inquiries or managing preferences. Does not store authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

MembershipPlan.title: MembershipPlan
MembershipPlan.description: Defines the different subscription tiers (Free, Standard, Featured) available for vendors, outlining pricing and features.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MembershipPlan entity (e.g., 'free', 'standard', 'featured').

name.description: The display name of the membership plan (e.g., 'FREE LISTING', 'STANDARD VENDOR').

description.description: A brief description or tagline for the membership plan.

monthlyPrice.description: The monthly price of the plan in Rands (ZAR), if applicable.

yearlyPrice.description: The yearly price of the plan in Rands (ZAR), if applicable.

features.description: A list of features included with this membership plan.

disabledFeatures.description: A list of features explicitly not included or disabled for this membership plan.

isRecommended.description: Indicates if this plan is recommended (e.g., 'STANDARD VENDOR').

isMostVisibility.description: Indicates if this plan offers the most visibility (e.g., 'FEATURED VENDOR').

sortOrder.description: A numeric value to determine the display order of the membership plans.

ServiceCategory.title: ServiceCategory
ServiceCategory.description: Defines distinct categories for wedding vendors (e.g., Photography, Venues, Catering). Used for classification and filtering.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ServiceCategory entity (e.g., 'photography', 'venues').

name.description: The display name of the service category (e.g., 'Photography', 'Wedding Venues').

description.description: A brief description of the service category.

Location.title: Location
Location.description: Defines geographical locations relevant to the marketplace, such as vendor operating regions or venue locations. Used for filtering and search.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Location entity (e.g., 'cape-town', 'johannesburg').

name.description: The display name of the location (e.g., 'Cape Town', 'Johannesburg').

description.description: A brief description or additional details for the location.

VendorApplication.title: VendorApplication
VendorApplication.description: Stores the information submitted by a prospective vendor during the application process, awaiting admin review.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VendorApplication entity.

ownerName.description: The name of the business owner or primary contact.

businessName.description: The registered name of the vendor's business.

email.description: The business's primary contact email address.

phoneNumber.description: The business's primary contact phone number.

websiteUrl.description: The official website URL for the vendor's business.

instagramHandle.description: The Instagram handle for the vendor's business (e.g., '@infaithjourney').

locationId.description: Reference to the primary Location where the vendor's business is based. (Relationship: Location 1:N VendorApplication)

categoryId.description: Reference to the primary ServiceCategory the vendor belongs to. (Relationship: ServiceCategory 1:N VendorApplication)

description.description: A short description of the vendor's business or services.

yearsInBusiness.description: The number of years the business has been operating.

pricingRange.description: A general indication of the vendor's pricing (e.g., 'R10,000 - R20,000', 'R50,000+').

servicesOffered.description: A detailed list of specific services or products offered by the vendor.

logoUrl.description: URL to the vendor's uploaded business logo in Firebase Storage.

coverImageUrl.description: URL to the vendor's uploaded cover image for their profile/application in Firebase Storage.

portfolioImageUrls.description: URLs to the vendor's uploaded portfolio images in Firebase Storage.

selectedPlanId.description: Reference to the MembershipPlan selected by the vendor during application. (Relationship: MembershipPlan 1:N VendorApplication)

howDidYouHearAboutUs.description: Information on how the vendor heard about InFaith Journey.

applicationStatus.description: The current status of the vendor application (e.g., 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the application was submitted.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the application was last updated.

Vendor.title: Vendor
Vendor.description: Represents an approved and active wedding vendor listed on the InFaith Journey marketplace.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Vendor entity. This may also correspond to the Firebase Authentication User ID.

businessName.description: The registered name of the vendor's business.

ownerName.description: The name of the business owner or primary contact.

email.description: The business's primary contact email address.

phoneNumber.description: The business's primary contact phone number.

websiteUrl.description: The official website URL for the vendor's business.

instagramHandle.description: The Instagram handle for the vendor's business (e.g., '@evergoldphotography').

locationIds.description: References to Locations where the vendor operates or provides services. (Relationship: Location N:N Vendor)

categoryIds.description: References to ServiceCategories that describe the vendor's services. (Relationship: ServiceCategory N:N Vendor)

description.description: A detailed 'About' section description for the vendor's profile page.

yearsInBusiness.description: The number of years the business has been operating.

pricingRange.description: A general indication of the vendor's pricing (e.g., 'R10,000 - R20,000', 'R50,000+').

servicesOffered.description: A checklist of specific services or packages offered by the vendor, displayed on their profile.

logoUrl.description: URL to the vendor's business logo, used for branding.

coverImageUrl.description: URL to the vendor's hero banner or cover image on their profile page.

portfolioImageUrls.description: URLs to the vendor's portfolio images, displayed in a gallery on their profile page.

membershipPlanId.description: Reference to the current MembershipPlan the vendor is subscribed to. (Relationship: MembershipPlan 1:N Vendor)

rating.description: The average rating of the vendor (e.g., 4.5 out of 5 stars).

reviewCount.description: The total number of reviews received by the vendor.

isApproved.description: Indicates if the vendor's profile has been approved by an administrator.

isActive.description: Indicates if the vendor's listing is currently active and visible on the marketplace.

isVerified.description: Indicates if the vendor has a 'Verified vendor badge'.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the vendor profile was created (e.g., upon approval of application).

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the vendor profile was last updated.

Venue.title: Venue
Venue.description: Represents a wedding venue listing on the marketplace, distinct from general service vendors.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Venue entity.

name.description: The display name of the wedding venue (e.g., 'Rosewood Manor').

description.description: A detailed description of the venue, its offerings, and amenities.

locationId.description: Reference to the primary Location of the venue. (Relationship: Location 1:N Venue)

capacityRange.description: A description of the venue's guest capacity (e.g., '100-200 guests', '200+').

budgetRange.description: A general indication of the venue's budget range (e.g., 'R80,000 - R150,000').

styleTags.description: A list of tags describing the architectural or aesthetic style of the venue (e.g., 'Vineyard', 'Garden', 'Beach', 'Estate').

imageUrl.description: URL to the main image for the venue, used for card display.

startingPrice.description: The starting price for booking the venue, in Rands (ZAR).

rating.description: The average rating of the venue (e.g., 4.5 out of 5 stars).

reviewCount.description: The total number of reviews received by the venue.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the venue listing was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the venue listing was last updated.

Inquiry.title: Inquiry
Inquiry.description: Stores requests for quotes or general inquiries sent by couples to vendors.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Inquiry entity.

vendorId.description: Reference to the Vendor to whom the inquiry is directed. (Relationship: Vendor 1:N Inquiry)

userProfileId.description: Optional reference to the UserProfile who sent the inquiry if they are logged in. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Inquiry)

inquirerName.description: The full name of the person sending the inquiry.

inquirerEmail.description: The email address of the person sending the inquiry.

inquirerPhoneNumber.description: The phone number of the person sending the inquiry.

message.description: The detailed message or request from the inquirer.

eventType.description: The type of event the inquiry is for (e.g., 'Wedding', 'Engagement').

eventDate.description: The planned date of the event, if provided.

inquiryType.description: The type of inquiry (e.g., 'Quote Request', 'General Inquiry').

status.description: The current status of the inquiry (e.g., 'new', 'viewed', 'replied', 'closed').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the inquiry was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the inquiry was last updated.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles for couples interacting with the marketplace. This path enforces path-based ownership, where the 'userId' parameter corresponds to the authenticated user's UID (request.auth.uid). Each document in this subcollection is privately owned by the 'userId' in the path. This design adheres to Authorization Independence as the owner is directly encoded in the path, simplifying security rules. QAP: Only the authenticated user can read/write their own profile.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication User ID (UID) of the user who owns this profile.

definition.description: Stores applications submitted by prospective vendors for review. Each document includes a denormalized 'submitterUid' field (which must match request.auth.uid) for Authorization Independence. This allows for atomic updates and simplified rules, avoiding 'get()' calls. QAP: Submitting user can read/update their own application; administrators can list and read all applications. Duplicate pending submissions for a user should be prevented at the application logic or rule level by checking the 'submitterUid' and 'applicationStatus' fields.

params.name: applicationId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific vendor application.

definition.description: Stores profiles of approved and active vendors. The 'vendorId' parameter corresponds to the vendor's Firebase Authentication UID, enforcing direct ownership. This denormalization simplifies rules for owner-specific updates. QAP: Publicly readable for all users to browse listings; only the owner (vendorId == request.auth.uid) or an administrator can modify their profile.

params.name: vendorId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication User ID (UID) of the approved vendor.

definition.description: Stores listings for wedding venues. This collection has a homogeneous security posture: publicly readable by all users for browsing. Write access is restricted to administrators only, ensuring data integrity. QAP: Publicly readable; administrators can manage venue listings.

params.name: venueId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific wedding venue listing.

definition.description: Stores inquiries sent from users (couples) to vendors. Each document includes denormalized 'vendorId' and 'userProfileId' (sender's UID) fields for Authorization Independence. This allows both the sender and the recipient vendor to access their relevant inquiries without complex 'get()' operations in rules. QAP: Only the sender (userProfileId) or the recipient vendor (vendorId) can read inquiries. Creation is permitted for authenticated users (with userProfileId matching request.auth.uid) or anonymous users (if userProfileId is null, and required contact info is provided).

params.name: inquiryId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific inquiry.

definition.description: Stores static configuration details for all membership plans (Free, Standard, Featured). This collection is publicly readable to allow all users to view and compare plans. Write access is restricted to administrators only. QAP: Publicly readable; administrators can manage plan definitions.

params.name: planId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific membership plan (e.g., 'free', 'standard', 'featured').

definition.description: Stores static definitions of service categories for vendors (e.g., Photography, Venues). This collection is publicly readable for display and filtering purposes. Write access is restricted to administrators only. QAP: Publicly readable; administrators can manage category definitions.

params.name: categoryId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific service category.

definition.description: Stores static definitions of geographical locations. This collection is publicly readable for display and filtering purposes. Write access is restricted to administrators only. QAP: Publicly readable; administrators can manage location definitions.

params.name: locationId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific geographical location.

definition.description: A dedicated collection for Database Access Control (DBAC) to signify administrator roles. The existence of a document at this path, where 'userId' is the authenticated user's UID, grants administrative privileges. This design uses 'Existence over Content' to simplify role checks in security rules. Authorization Independence is maintained as the role is checked directly via path existence, not content. QAP: Readable only by the owner (for internal checks by client-side admin dashboards) and writable by other administrators for management.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique Firebase Authentication User ID (UID) of the user who holds the administrator role.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following the core principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC, QAPs, and Invariants, alongside the mandated strategies for security, scalability, and debuggability. The primary goal is to minimize complexity in security rules and ensure robust authorization.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**

1.  **Vendor Applications (`/vendorApplications/{applicationId}`):** Each `VendorApplication` document explicitly includes a `submitterUid` field. This field stores the Firebase Authentication UID of the user who submitted the application. Security rules can directly compare `request.auth.uid` with `resource.data.submitterUid` without performing any `get()` operations on parent collections or other documents, ensuring atomic authorization checks. This is crucial for creating and managing applications. Admins, identified by the `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection, can also access these documents. This setup also facilitates preventing duplicate pending applications by allowing application logic or security rules to query for existing pending applications by `submitterUid`.
2.  **Vendors (`/vendors/{vendorId}`):** The document ID `{vendorId}` for each `Vendor` document is set to the vendor's Firebase Authentication UID. This inherently denormalizes ownership directly into the path and document ID. Rules can simply check `request.auth.uid == vendorId` for write operations by the owner, completely eliminating `get()` calls for ownership verification.
3.  **Inquiries (`/inquiries/{inquiryId}`):** Each `Inquiry` document includes `senderUid` (the UID of the user who sent the inquiry) and `vendorId` (the UID of the vendor receiving it). This denormalization allows both the sender and the recipient to access their relevant inquiries independently by checking `request.auth.uid` against either `resource.data.senderUid` or `resource.data.vendorId`. This avoids `get()` operations for cross-entity authorization.
4.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}/profile`):** By nesting `UserProfile` documents under `/users/{userId}`, where `{userId}` is the authenticated user's UID, ownership is embedded in the path. Rules verify `request.auth.uid == userId` for direct, atomic authorization.
5.  **Admin Roles (`/roles_admin/{userId}`):** Admin roles are determined by the *existence* of a document where `userId` matches `request.auth.uid`. This 'Existence over Content' approach is an explicit form of denormalization for role-based access, enabling direct checks like `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` without reading document contents.

**Querying for Authorization Posture (QAPs):**

1.  **Homogeneous Security Posture & Public Readability:** Collections like `membershipPlans`, `serviceCategories`, `locations`, `vendors`, and `venues` are designed for public readability. All documents within these collections share the same security requirements for reading (i.e., anyone can read). This enables secure `list` operations without relying on security rules to filter results, as rules will simply `allow read` for everyone. Write access for these collections is typically restricted to administrators, ensuring data integrity.
2.  **User-Specific & Admin-Accessible Lists:**
    *   `vendorApplications`: Security rules will allow an authenticated user to `list` applications where `submitterUid == request.auth.uid`. Additionally, administrators (checked via `/roles_admin`) can `list` all applications. This satisfies QAPs by ensuring lists are pre-filtered by the user's role/ownership without relying on client-side filtering being enforced by rules.
    *   `inquiries`: Both the sender (`senderUid`) and the recipient vendor (`vendorId`) can `list` their respective inquiries. Security rules enforce that `list` queries must include filters (`where('senderUid', '==', request.auth.uid)` or `where('vendorId', '==', request.auth.uid)`) to match the requesting user's UID, upholding QAPs.

This architecture ensures that security rules are straightforward, concise, and do not incur performance penalties or complexity from cross-document `get()` calls. It also clearly defines access patterns, enhancing debuggability and maintaining data integrity through explicit ownership and state modeling fields.
